commits.subject: net: fixed TWebSocketAsyncServer.WebSocketBroadcast deadlock when a send fails
commits.body:
- the connection handles are now retrieved within ConnectionLock, and the frames are sent outside of it via ConnectionFind()
- a failing Write() calls ConnectionDelete() and its WriteLock on the same TRWLock, which can't be upgraded from a ReadOnlyLock
- document this constraint on ConnectionFindAndLock(), Connection[] and SendDirect()

commits.subject: core: introducing IntelAvx512 to detect AVX-512 support enabled by the OS
commits.body:
CpuFeatures reflects the raw CPUID bits, so AVX-512 flags may be set even if
the OS does not save the opmask/ZMM registers at context switch (e.g. on old
Windows or within some VMs): executing any EVEX opcode then triggers #UD.
Unlike AVX/AVX2, there was no XCR0 check for the AVX-512 state.

- new IsZmmOSEnabled asm on x86 and x64, checking XCR0 bits 1-2 and 5-7
- new IntelAvx512 function, returning CpuFeatures * CPUAVX512FEATURES, or []
  if the OS did not enable the whole AVX-512 state
- new CPUAVX512FEATURES and CPUAVX512X64V4 (x86-64-v4 level) constants
- new cpuAVX512 flag in X64CpuFeatures, set at x86-64-v4 level

CpuFeatures itself is not modified, since it is part of the GetComputerUuid
hash: clearing its AVX-512 bits would change the computer UUID on such
systems.

Validated on Intel i7-1255U (no AVX-512, XCR0=$07) and AMD Ryzen 9 8945HS
(Zen 4 under Hyper-V, XCR0=$E7) with Win32 and Win64 executables actually
running a vpaddd zmm opcode, and TTestCoreBase passing on Win64.
